column4: Yes, the mechanism differs by context. In G0692 (Matt.20.3/6) the mechanism is circumstantial/economic -- absence of an employer's summons. In 1Tim.5.13/Titus.1.12 (G0692, cluster context) idleness operates via habitual moral choice leading to further vice. In H8220 (Eccl.10.18) the mechanism is physical/instrumental -- slack hands failing to maintain a structure, producing direct material decay. In G0691 (2Pet.2.3) the 'mechanism' is rhetorical/theological -- a personification denying dormancy to underscore the certainty of divine judgment's operation. Four distinct registers (economic, moral, physical, theological-rhetorical) for the same root concept.
